findings.problem: Pinned Tonic unary/server-streaming consumes the first inbound message then trailers() drains the rest. The prior claim that upstream rejects multiple messages was false and could discard input before business dispatch.
findings.resolution: An explicit fresh per-request mode-aware Decoder accepts one complete message for unary/server-streaming and returns INVALID_ARGUMENT on a second before Handler execution; empty framed message valid, zero messages retains INTERNAL. Client-stream mode allows multiple messages with independent quotas. Native Tonic framing/decompression remains reused.
findings.independent_verification: Read pinned Grpc.map_request_unary and Streaming.trailers; wrote a separate five-test public-API regression, executed Linux Rust1.100 --locked, all five passed. Read corrected author code and six additional test cases, all19 author Linux cases passed.

findings.problem: Residual C# route and managed-app wording could imply managed routing or a managed Server fallback.
findings.resolution: C# declares routes/Handlers; Rust performs route matching and dispatch. Only applications not using Server can omit the native Server package.

findings.problem: request_dispatch(owner,header_owner) left callback payload ownership inconsistent with Core notification/typed-take separation.
findings.resolution: Callback borrows cookie/handler_id/ticket notification only. Admitted dispatcher uses request_take_context outside callback for exactly-once atomic transfer of named request/header owners, null outputs on failure; native pending storage/leases/budgets survive queued notification, failure/cancel/shutdown converge on one cleanup.

findings.problem: Two source range ends exceeded actual EOF by one line.
findings.resolution: DOTNET-MOBILE11 ends at91 and RUST-ANDROID at72; exact full-file hashes/Git blobs remain unchanged.

findings.problem: Original Windows allocation probe failed while first clock initialization was inside measured allocation region; numerical observation was after assertion and therefore absent.
findings.resolution: Clock/allocation counter warmup moved outside measured loop; allocation end read before elapsed formatting; observation printed before assertions. Original Windows failure/logs remain preserved. Corrected Linux11 assertions and zero current-thread loop allocation are real; no Windows corrected outcome is inferred in this review version.
findings.independent_verification: Read original failed Windows stdout/stderr and corrected full source plus actual Linux raw stdout; verifies measurement scope, not universal zero allocations or production timing.
